As a consequence of all preceding items, operating income was $435.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to an operating income of $379.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Tasman (5,936 TEU, built 2000), Akiteta (2,220 TEU, built 2002), and Keta (2,207 TEU, built 2003) were sold for an aggregate gain of $28.3 million in the first quarter of 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in P2 (20-F Risk Factors) and P4 (6-K MD&A)
competitive_position.claim: With a TEU-weighted average fleet age of 18.4 years, fleet aging threatens to drive operating costs above normal inflation and reduce future revenue unless vessels are replaced.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, we owned 71 vessels, with a total carrying capacity of 423,020 TEU with an average age, weighted by TEU capacity, of 18.4 years.
As our fleet ages, we may incur increased operating costs beyond normal inflation, which would adversely affect our results of operations.

Unless we set aside reserves or are able to borrow funds for vessel replacement, at the end of the useful lives of our vessels our revenue will decline, which would adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in P2 (20-F Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Although global idle capacity was 0.8% at year-end 2025, a 34.5% global containership orderbook-to-fleet ratio poses a threat of vessel oversupply that could depress charter hire rates and profitability.
quotes: As at December 31, 2025, idle capacity of the global containership fleet was 0.8%, and the global containership orderbook to fleet ratio was 34.5%, which was weighted heavily towards containerships larger than 10,000 TEU.
An over-supply of containership capacity may lead to reductions in charter hire rates and profitability.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in P2 (20-F Risk Factors) and P3 (20-F Item 5)
competitive_position.claim: Re-chartering exposure threatens future revenues because GSL may be unable to recharter vessels at profitable rates upon time charter expiry in weaker market conditions.
quotes: We may be unable to recharter our vessels at profitable rates, if at all, upon their time charter expiry.

The time charters for three of our 71 containerships either have expired or could expire before the end of the first half of 2026, and a further six vessels have charters that could expire during the second half of 2026.
The charter rate that we will be able to achieve on renewal will be affected by market conditions at that time.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in P2 (20-F Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Because time charter payments are GSL's sole source of operating cash flow, charterer defaults or non-performance could severely reduce revenues and leave vessels unchartered while fixed expenses continue.
quotes: Payments to us by our charterers under time charters are, and will continue to be, our sole source of operating cash flow.
If we lose a time charter because the charterer is unable to pay us or for any other reason, we may be unable to re-deploy the related vessel on similar terms or at all.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in P2 (20-F Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: GSL faces competition for charters and vessel acquisitions from rivals with larger fleets, greater financial resources, and a lower cost of capital, while industry financing for containerships has been limited and costly.
quotes: Many of these competitors may have greater financial resources and a lower cost of capital than us, may operate larger fleets, may have been established for longer, and may be able to offer better charter rates.
In recent years, financing for investment in containerships, whether newbuildings or existing vessels, has been severely limited.
Further, the cost of available financing is currently high and may increase significantly in the future.

the disruptions of shipping routes, including due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, lower water levels in the Panama Canal and the ongoing attacks by Houthis in the Red Sea;

Our Executive Chairman also beneficially owns approximately 7.9% of our Class A common shares.

The fees and expenses payable pursuant to our technical and commercial ship management agreements with Technomar and Conchart, respectively, will be payable without regard to our business, results of operation, and financial condition and we have limited rights to terminate our management agreements.

quotes: Volatility of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) could affect our profitability, earnings, and cash flows.

In December 2021, we entered into a USD one-month London Interbank Offered Rate (“LIBOR”) interest rate cap of 0.75% through fourth quarter of 2026 on $484.1 million of floating rate debt and in February 2022 we entered into USD one-month LIBOR interest rate caps of 0.75% though fourth quarter of 2026 on $507.9 million of floating rate debt to hedge our cash flows.
